searchText: Question: Why has development of an EIP (969/3369/3372) to remove asics from the network been left to the community instead of ether devs working on this issue, when the ether white paper clearly states that the network should not allow asic mining? Ethereum development is decentralized. Devs are free to work on issues they believe in or are interested in. Seems like most current core devs believes the merge is a more beneficial step to take rather than focusing on those aforemention EIPs. On the other hand, if anyone does wish to push that EIP forward to the core devs and is willing to take the time and effort to see it until realization, then you may see some success in getting those implemented. I don't think there's an issue with time/effort amongst supporters of such change, but the lack of technical knowledge is severely hampering work. Is there no one here that recognises the danger posed by the centralisation of mining amongst asic operators *in the meantime before 2.0* which is slated for ~15 months away I believe From an outside perspective it really looks like ethereum is asleep at the wheel when it comes to this issue. I was one of a few campaigning for this to be looked at back when the 1559-mining channel was open. There was basically radio silence when it was brought up time and again. Then eventually we were told 'you do it'. We don't know how There's almost no chance of getting core dev buy in on 969/3369/3372 (I'm assuming those are progpow and the like). The merge and transition to proof of stake eliminate asics and are being actively worked on. Not progpow. The house is on fire but it's OK because our new house will be built in 15 months 🤦🏻‍♂️ oh well Thx <dankrad> The problem is that removing ASICs actually reduces the security of the network <dankrad> This probably wasn't clear back when the whitepaper was written, but overall, the tendency is to believe that a network with ASIC mining is safer than without, that's why progpow never had that much support. Now obviously with the merge coming closer the issue is moot This is very hyperbolic. The best way to be heard here is to present a compelling case (especially when it's related to mining where lots of people tend to have financial motivations) Also 15 months seems unlikely <dankrad> It will be much faster than 15 months For some value of “much” ... between 8 and 3 months faster, maybe. Where 8 faster seems unlikely, and 3 faster is quite cautious
